chunks: What Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq Shaʿīr, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
Going out on the Day of al-Fiṭr and the Day of al-Aḍḥā to the open prayer-ground is good for one who is able to go out to it.
So I said: Tell me, if he is ill and unable to go out, should he pray in his house? He said: No.
So the correct view concerning it also is what we have said: that this is not an obligatory duty upon him; rather, it is only on the basis of recommendation and desirability.

key_terms.الْجَبَّانَةِ: the open prayer-ground outside the town
key_terms.الْخُرُوجُ: going out for the Eid prayer
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: a sick person unable to attend

ai.seo_question: Is the Eid prayer obligatory for someone who cannot go out to the prayer-ground?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that going out for the Eid prayer to the prayer-ground is recommended for those who are able. It also shows that the Eid prayer is not individually obligatory in this context, since one who is ill and unable to go out is not instructed to perform it at home.
